title: Bounded Temporal-Certificate Cost and Reference Runtime Overhead Characterization
purpose: Measure and characterize only the incremental compute and transient-memory cost of the already-qualified reference-Richards temporal certificate machinery, without selecting a head budget, changing physics, changing solver fidelity, or defining a performance policy.

qualified_dependency.dependency_nonclaim_preserved: F-VQ34 does not select, recommend or qualify a numeric H_budget for any application.

included: optional accepted right-derivative history snapshot and replacement
reference constitutive reevaluation performed by the temporal indicator
one defect reference_tridag solve when previous derivative history is available and the indicator envelope is admitted
scalar normalization by an already-supplied valid H_budget
runtime diagnostic and transaction-outcome counter propagation
incremental transient allocation/copy cost attributable to the temporal service
excluded: selection, recommendation or optimization of H_budget
changes to physical configuration or physical process options
changes to the reference Richards nonlinear algorithm or tolerances

source_bound_inventory.role: F-KT-owned optional continuation carrier; replace and snapshot allocate and copy O(n) derivative vectors; payload is explicitly not physical state and does not enter storage or mass accounting.

Computes current derivative, constitutive/operator terms, raw defect, one reference_tridag correction and head_inf_bound; declares additional_full_nonlinear_solves=0 and additional_tridiagonal_solves=1 after the defect solve is invoked.
Owns reference_tridag; forward elimination and backward substitution are combined in one routine, so factorization is not separately observable on the defect path.
Defines principal-solver diagnostics and temporal-indicator result counters.

Selects temporal-history service from numerical_continuation_layout_id, calls the principal reference solve once per model advance, invokes temporal service after convergence, accumulates the extra tridiagonal solve into outcome linear_solves, replaces accepted trial history, and normalizes head_inf_bound by the supplied budget.
Provides TX_TEMPORAL_NONE for an A/B timing route that keeps transaction acceptance independent of the certificate while the runtime temporal service can still execute.
Frozen qualified fixture family and positive test-oracle budget construction; VALID_ACCEPT uses H_budget=2*direct_Binf only to force C_h=0.5 in qualification and is not an application budget policy.

paired_runtime_design.purpose: Isolate full temporal-service overhead without certificate-driven accept/reject/retry differences.
same_in_both_arms: parameter_set_id and all physical parameter values
reference Richards numerical tolerances and iteration limits
canonical numerical configuration including the positive test-oracle budget value
single-attempt transaction policy and mass tolerance

arm_B_active.previous_right_derivative: seeded from the same frozen source-bound fixture construction used by F-VQ34
arm_B_active.budget: reuse the corresponding frozen F-VQ34 positive test-oracle budget construction unchanged; PE06 must not tune, select or rank it

paired_runtime_design.why_TX_TEMPORAL_NONE: The model still executes the temporal service when the history layout is enabled, but transaction acceptance does not consume C_h. Therefore A and B can have the same accepted trial count and physical step fate, avoiding a retry/rollback confounder.
paired_runtime_design.timing_order: balanced ABBA blocks with A/B roles otherwise unchanged
paired_runtime_design.warmup: execute untimed warmup blocks before every measured compiler/case block
paired_runtime_design.timing_unit: time batches large enough to dominate clock resolution; report per-trial values from fixed batch counts
paired_runtime_design.production_matrix: reuse the frozen 12-case F-VQ34 hydraulic matrix; no post-result case changes
paired_runtime_design.synthetic_size_sweep: optional for O(n) complexity/allocation characterization only; never production acceptance evidence

required_pre_timing_equivalence_gates: A and B each execute exactly one principal Richards trajectory per attempt
A and B attempts, retries and rollback counts are identical
A and B principal nonlinear_iterations are identical
A and B principal jacobian_builds are identical
A and B principal backtracking_attempts and internal_retries are identical
B observation reports temporal_additional_tridiagonal_solves=1 on admitted seeded-history cases
B total linear_solves equals A total linear_solves+1 when all principal-solver diagnostics are equal
A and B candidate physical pressure_head, water_content, ponding_depth and groundwater_level are bitwise identical
A and B physical mass accounting and residual are bitwise identical
only B carries the optional accepted derivative continuation payload

metrics.principal_full_nonlinear_trajectories: required via headcalc_calls/attempts and exact A/B equality
metrics.defect_tridiagonal_solves: required separately through temporal observation and A/B delta
metrics.history_snapshot_replace_operations: required structural count; allocation/copy timing may be measured in a component microbenchmark
metrics.normalization_operations: required structural count; scalar normalization timing may be measured only as part of temporal service unless clock resolution permits isolation
metrics.allocations: report only with reliable instrumentation; otherwise report source-bound allocation sites and O(n) transient shape without invented byte counts
metrics.scratch_bytes: report only from reliable type/array accounting; no persistent per-column scratch may be introduced

component_microbenchmarks.rule: fixed vector sizes and fixed iteration counts; source-bound O(n) allocation/copy characterization only
use a precomputed converged solve_result so the principal nonlinear solve is not included in component timing
retain the frozen positive test-oracle budget construction; no H_budget policy inference is permitted

H1.statement: Enabling the admitted temporal service adds zero full nonlinear Richards trajectories.
H1.source_support: indicator sets additional_full_nonlinear_solves=0 and backend invokes service only after the converged principal solve

H2.statement: An admitted seeded-history temporal evaluation adds exactly one combined defect reference_tridag solve.
H2.source_support: one reference_tridag call followed by additional_tridiagonal_solves=1

H3.statement: Under TX_TEMPORAL_NONE, enabling temporal-history/certificate machinery leaves the physical candidate and strict mass result bitwise unchanged.

H4.statement: The incremental temporal-service transient work is O(n) in vertical node count for the currently admitted reference-Richards envelope.
H4.source_support: history and indicator allocate/copy/assemble a fixed number of length-n vectors and reference_tridag is a single forward/backward sweep

reporting_rules: Separate source-declared solve counters from empirically observed runtime counters.
Separate component timing from end-to-end paired runtime timing.
Do not subtract or name a defect factorization cost separately because reference_tridag exposes no separate factorization event.
Report O0 and O2 independently before any pooled summary.
A finite benchmark matrix characterizes observed wall-clock tails; it does not establish a universal hardware-independent time bound.
Any failure of physical or mass identity invalidates performance interpretation and must stop qualification.
Synthetic size sweeps may support complexity statements only and cannot replace the qualified real-Richards fixture matrix.

architecture_invariant_audit.3_explicit_data_separation: REQUIRED: temporal budget remains numerical configuration; history remains optional numerical continuation data, not physical storage.
architecture_invariant_audit.5_scratch_per_worker: REQUIRED: indicator transient arrays and solver workspace remain transient/worker-local; no PE06 persistent scratch is admitted.
architecture_invariant_audit.7_transactional_timesteps: REQUIRED: benchmark configuration may not bypass checkpoint/trial/commit semantics; TX_TEMPORAL_NONE is used only to remove certificate acceptance as an A/B timing confounder.
architecture_invariant_audit.9_generic_time: REQUIRED: reuse non-calendar [t0,t1] fixture horizons; no day-boundary assumption.
architecture_invariant_audit.13_mass_conservation_absolute: HARD GATE: A/B strict physical mass result must remain identical; performance evidence is void if mass semantics differ.
architecture_invariant_audit.23_physics_solver_policy_separated: HARD GATE: only numerical continuation layout differs between A/B; physical options and reference solver settings do not.
architecture_invariant_audit.24_predictable_compute: TARGET: quantify fixed extra trajectory/linear-solve shape and observed overhead/tails; no universal wall-clock guarantee from a finite matrix.
architecture_invariant_audit.25_reference_mode_available: PASS BY SCOPE: only the qualified reference Richards path is characterized.
architecture_invariant_audit.26_runtime_diagnostics: REQUIRED: use existing solve/temporal counters and preserve provenance of all timing rows.
architecture_invariant_audit.30_architecture_change_audit: REQUIRED: any instrumentation source change must be reconciled here before evidence is accepted.

forbidden_claims: PE06 does not select or recommend H_budget.
PE06 does not define BALANCED or THROUGHPUT solver policy.
PE06 does not qualify a production speedup.
PE06 does not permit a physical-fidelity or mass-conservation concession.
PE06 does not infer a universal wall-clock bound from finite hardware measurements.
PE06 is not qualified until the paired O0/O2 runtime matrix and equivalence gates are persisted and independently reproducible.
